title: Bless the place (Berakhot 54a)
hook: blessings on seeing a place where a miracle happened to you
tomorrow: why would heart be spelled with an extra letter?

segments.voice: Last time, the soul enjoys scent: a pleasure the body doesn't share, so it gets a blessing. Today, a blessing for a patch of road.
screen: `THE SOUL ENJOYS SCENT.` → `A PATCH OF ROAD.`

segments.voice: There's an intersection most people drive through without a thought, and one person never does, because that's where the other car missed them. Now a road called Ever Yemina, in the Talmud. A man is walking it alone. A lion comes at him. And then, the Talmud says only, a miracle was done for him, and he was saved. He walks away shaking. And he doesn't know what to do with the road.
screen: `THE CAR THAT MISSED.` → `A LION ON THE ROAD.` → `A MIRACLE, AND HE'S SAVED.`

segments.voice: So he goes to Rava, a sage, and Rava tells him: every time you come to that place, say a blessing, blessed is the One who did a miracle for me in this place. Not once. Every time. The Mishnah already had a blessing like it for places where miracles happened to the whole people, the sea, the river, the walls. Here the Talmud brings it down to one person's road. The road where he almost died becomes the road where he blesses. Then a second sage, Mar son of Ravina, with two close calls. Once, in the valley of Aravot, thirsty, a well of water appeared for him. Another time, in the market of Mechoza, a wild camel charged him, and a wall split open, and he ducked inside. Here's the detail worth telling a friend tonight. When he came to Aravot, he blessed for the well and for the camel. When he came to Mechoza, for the camel and for the well. In each place he named both rescues. One place where you were helped opens the memory of all of them. So why would a man bless the road where a lion jumped him? Because that's where he was saved.
screen: `EVERY TIME YOU COME THERE.` · `FROM A PEOPLE TO ONE ROAD.` · `A WELL, A CAMEL, A WALL.` · `IN EACH PLACE, BOTH RESCUES.` · then, large: `BLESS THE PLACE.`

segments.voice: Choose one place where you were helped: a hospital hallway, a friend's couch, a roadside, a classroom. Go back there in your mind and stand in it until you can see the light. Then decide when you'll pass it next, and what you'll say when you do.
screen: `ONE PLACE YOU WERE HELPED.` · `STAND IN IT.` · `WHEN WILL YOU PASS IT NEXT?`

segments.voice: Bless the place: Rava's answer to the man saved from a lion, a blessing every time he came back to that road.
For the road home: bless the place, and every rescue comes back with it. That's thirty-three.

screen: `DAY 1520 COUNTS.` → `BERAKHOT · 33 OF 50.` → `TOMORROW: WHY SPELL HEART WITH AN EXTRA LETTER?`

howItsDone: Jewish law gives a blessing on seeing a place where a miracle was done for the Jewish people, and another for a place where a person was miraculously saved: 'who did a miracle for me in this place.'

match.prompt: the rescues and the roads — tap the pairs.
pairs: a well for a thirsty man
a camel, and a wall that split
bless every time you come there

myth: the place-blessing is only for miracles that happened to a whole people
the Talmud brings it to one person's road: a miracle for me in this place.
Mar son of Ravina named both of his rescues in each place
at Aravot, the well and the camel; at Mechoza, the camel and the well.
Rava told the man to say the blessing once, the next time he passed
every time he came to that place.

fork.setup: your mom always goes quiet driving past the hospital where you were born early and spent weeks in the NICU. your brother says it's morbid and she should take another road. what would Rava say?
options: your brother's right: it's healthier to avoid places tied to fear.
keep the road, and let it be the place where she blesses.
pass it once more, say goodbye, and then stop thinking about it.
fork.reveal: Rava tells the man saved from the lion to bless the place every time he comes there: the road of the danger becomes the road of thanks.

original.note: Hebrew: miracle; 'who did a miracle for me in this place.'

trapdoor: what you thought: some places are holy, and you bless them.
what it means: any place where you were saved becomes a place to bless, every time you pass.

what a scholar hears: Mishnah Berakhot 9:1 gives the blessing for miracles to Israel; the Gemara on 54a extends it to an individual through Rava and the lion at Ever Yemina, and Mar son of Ravina's two rescues.
guess: a blessing where you were saved, said every time you return
a prayer to make a new house or room safe to live in
a blessing said once, the day you first arrive somewhere
recall: the blessing hands the gift to you

chat.says: saba's follow-up today. he stopped at the hospital doors and said thank you out loud. to a building??
options: Rava told a man saved from a lion to bless that road. It's where Saba was helped.
Blessings are only for holy places, so he must have meant the doctors.
He's probably just glad to be out. Places don't get thanked in Judaism.
chat.meaning: On Berakhot 54a, Rava tells the man saved on the road to bless every time he comes to that place. The place of rescue becomes a place of thanks.

Mar son of Ravina.meaning: a sage saved twice: by a well and by a wall

Mishnah.meaning: the early collection of Jewish law the Talmud discusses

sources.ref: Mishnah Berakhot 9:1 (one who sees a place where miracles were done for Israel)
Babylonian Talmud, Berakhot 54a (the man and the lion at Ever Yemina; Rava: 'who did a miracle for me in this place'; Mar son of Ravina at Aravot and Mechoza)
